question: What is the main root cause of inherited degenerative diseases?

options.A: Genetic mutations passed down within families
options.C: Bacterial infections in the nervous system
options.D: Sudden physical trauma to the brain

explanation: You've got this! These conditions happen because of changes in the genes passed down from parents, leading to gradual tissue breakdown over time. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h1)

question: How do inherited degenerative diseases usually progress compared to a sudden injury?

options.A: They alternate randomly between extreme health and sudden failure
options.B: They remain completely stable after the initial onset
options.C: They start quietly and worsen slowly over a long period
options.D: They appear overnight and resolve completely on their own

explanation: Think of it as a slow burn. Unlike sudden accidents, degenerative conditions develop gradually over months or years. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h1)

question: Which sign often shows up earliest in an inherited degenerative disease?

options.A: Complete paralysis of both lower limbs
options.B: Mild clumsiness and a slight loss of balance
options.C: Total loss of long-term childhood memories

explanation: Early signs are usually very subtle—like a minor stumble or slight coordination issue that is easy to brush off at first. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h2)

question: Why are early symptoms like mild memory slips and tiredness often tricky to diagnose right away?

options.A: They always appear alongside total paralysis
options.B: They disappear completely within twenty-four hours
options.C: They only occur during strenuous physical exercise
options.D: They easily mimic normal aging and everyday tiredness

explanation: It's easy to miss the early clues because they look just like everyday stress, fatigue, or getting older! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h2)

question: In degenerative conditions, what does muscle spasticity mean?

options.C: Complete limpness of all skeletal muscles
options.D: Sudden swelling of the joints from fluid

explanation: Spasticity is just a medical way of saying the muscles are tight and stiff because nerve damage interferes with smooth movement. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h3)

question: Why is an unsteady walk (gait instability) such a big worry for patients with nerve degeneration?

options.A: It prevents the patient from speaking clearly
options.B: It triggers sudden spikes in blood pressure
options.C: It greatly increases the risk of dangerous falls and injury
options.D: It causes immediate permanent blindness in both eyes

explanation: When balance is off, walking safely becomes a daily challenge. As nurses, keeping our patients safe from falls is a huge priority! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h3)

question: Which mental ability tends to fade first in degenerative brain conditions?
explanation: Recent memories are usually affected long before older, deeply rooted childhood memories start to fade. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h4)

question: What does a decline in 'executive function' look like for a patient?

options.A: Trouble with planning, organizing, and solving problems
options.B: Constant involuntary shaking of the hands
options.C: A complete inability to feel physical pain
options.D: Sudden loss of the ability to swallow food

explanation: Executive functions are like the brain's manager—they help us plan our day, organize tasks, and solve everyday problems. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT an automatic (autonomic) body process linked to nerve degeneration?

options.B: Sudden mastery of complex math skills
options.C: Drastic blood pressure drops when standing

explanation: You definitely don't gain superpowers from nerve degeneration! Autonomic functions control automatic things like blood pressure and sweating. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h5)

question: Why can autonomic nerve failure cause a patient to feel dizzy when standing up?

options.A: The inner ear fills with fluid from poor circulation
options.B: Blood pressure drops drastically because vessels fail to constrict
options.C: Eye muscles become too weak to focus on light
options.D: Brain cells instantly run out of oxygen and die

explanation: Normally, your nerves quickly tighten your blood vessels when you stand up to keep blood flowing to your head. When those nerves fail, blood pressure drops and you feel dizzy. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h5)

question: What is the medical term for trouble swallowing in advanced degenerative diseases?
explanation: Dysphagia means difficulty swallowing. Spotting this early helps us protect patients from choking or getting food in their lungs! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h6)

question: For a bedridden patient with advanced nerve degeneration, what is a nurse mainly trying to prevent by turning them regularly?
explanation: When patients can't shift their own weight in bed, pressure sores can form quickly. Frequent turning is one of our most important nursing duties! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h6)

question: Why is continuous, long-term monitoring so essential when caring for patients with degenerative conditions?

options.A: It completely stops the underlying genetic mutation from spreading
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: It guarantees the patient will regain full physical strength
options.D: It helps catch slow, steady declines and new complications early

explanation: Because these diseases creep up slowly over time, keeping a close eye on the patient helps us catch new problems right away and step in to help. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h7)

question: Which of these is a key nursing action when assessing someone with a degenerative disease?

options.B: Reversing the genetic mutation in the laboratory
options.D: Evaluating motor strength and skin integrity

explanation: Spot on! As nurses, we keep a close watch on muscle strength, movement, and skin health to keep our patients as safe and comfortable as possible. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h7)
